l7yttw:
Our Accounting & Finance BSc provides a hands on experience of financial study, developing skills to take into any financial career.

Accounting & Finance at King’s College London covers foundations of general management as well as accounting and finance in the first year while offering more specialist content throughout the rest of the degree. The accounting and finance focus becomes more pronounced in the second and third years of the course, where a number of more advanced modules in financial reporting, management accounting, asset management, auditing, corporate finance and taxation will be offered.

There are two things that are unique about studying accounting and finance at King’s: one is the strong grounding in a broad, social science-based approach to learning; the other is a keen emphasis on the way in which financial careers are being reshaped by technological innovation. This dual focus on social science and technological innovation translates into a concern to cultivate accounting and finance graduates that are socially rounded and technologically adept.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

titb3f:
Study for a BSc Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology degree at King's College London.

The Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology BSc degree course offers you an opportunity to explore how the human body is constructed, how anatomical structures function normally and the basis of human diseases caused when these structures do not form properly or become damaged.

You will learn how our anatomy has emerged through the study of evolution, embryonic development, anatomical structure-function relationships and ageing. In doing so, you will consider how human anatomy is constructed and functions normally at the organismal, tissue, cellular and molecular levels.

We are one of only a few UK universities to offer an Anatomy BSc programme. Our students have access to extensive, modern dissection room facilities and the Gordon Museum of Pathology. Our course is research-led, providing an opportunity for you to study human anatomy in depth and to integrate this knowledge with cutting-edge research in anatomy, embryology, evolution, cell and molecular biology. You will learn how these rapidly advancing and interlinked fields of scientific investigation are helping us better understand how the human body works and the origins of many human diseases.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
pive6f:
Anatomy, Developmental and Human Biology Intercalated BSc online prospectus

The Anatomy, Developmental & Human Biology Intercalated BSc offers students already on medical degree programmes the opportunity to achieve an additional specialist degree in just one year. The programme will help you to develop critical scientific research skills, and gain knowledge of a diverse range of anatomy-related fields. These include applied and clinical anatomy, ageing, regenerative medicine topics, genetics, cell and developmental biology, neuroscience, psychology and behavioural science, which reflect the teaching strengths of the department and wider School of Biosciences.

It offers a wide choice of taught units, including advanced human anatomy, biology of cancer, developmental neurobiology and psychology/behavioral science. You are also required to complete a compulsory research project, either library-based or experimental, on topics that reflect the research strengths and interests of the department.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

Study Artificial Intelligence BSc at King's College London.

Our BSc in Artificial Intelligence will provide you with a comprehensive and cutting-edge understanding of AI theory and practice. AI significantly affects people’s lives, and it is encountered in more and more of our daily activities. These include activities such as using smart devices, digital voice assistants, and travel aids, as well as banking online or receiving personalised recommendations about movies to rent.

Our programme is structured around AI's core dimensions, including the foundations of AI, data science and Machine Learning. You’ll study reasoning, interactions and autonomous agents including robotics. You'll also gain a deep understanding of the ethics and philosophy of AI and its shifting role in society through exploring the social, legal, and professional dimensions. Throughout your degree, you’ll apply your skillset to tackle complex projects inspired by real-world industry problems. This could include working with an external company on developing a tech solution to an industry problem in your third year.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).

Study our Arts in AI & Data in Culture and Society MA in the Department of Digital Humanities in the Faculty of Arts & Humanities, King's College London

Explore how AI and data are transforming culture, society, politics and everyday life. AI is increasingly embedded in everyday life, from chatbots and image generation to recommendation algorithms and autonomous agents. As these technologies develop, they raise important questions about privacy, power and the evolving relationship between humans and machines.

Our MA in AI and Data in Culture and Society explores how AI is reshaping social, cultural, political and economic processes and generating knowledge. You’ll examine how data are transformed into representations, models and forms of machine memory that shape what AI systems can know, predict and do.

This research-driven multidisciplinary programme combines technical skills with humanities and social science perspectives. You’ll learn to collect and analyse data, programme in Python (including AI assisted coding), use emerging AI tools and assistants and explore machine learning concepts, including representations, embeddings and model behaviour. You’ll also examine the legal and policy frameworks shaping AI and data, including through a module taught by The Dickson Poon School of Law.

Source: the university's official course page (www.kcl.ac.uk).
